flags: Oportun formally introduced 'Oportun Forward,' a new strategy to simplify its core business and drive durable growth, and announced the additions of Bill Franklin as Chief Financial Officer, Bernardo Martinez as Chief Retail and Sales Officer, and Garrett Hope as Chief Product Officer.

Oportun raised its full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting total revenue of $955 to $960 million, an Annualized Net Charge-Off Rate of 11.6% plus or minus 10 basis points, and Adjusted EPS of $1.60 to $1.70, reflecting 21% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
The Board appointed William Franklin as Chief Financial Officer and principal financial officer, effective September 8, 2026, replacing Joseph Schueller in that role.

The Board appointed Mr. Scheirman as Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee and as a member of the Compensation & Leadership Committee.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) and P5 (10-Q Risk Factors); the two-partner structure is stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A).
risks.claim: Oportun's origination channel is concentrated in one or two bank partners; loss of either would materially impair loan originations.
quotes: In the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, Pathward originated approximately 98% and 92% of aggregate personal loan originations, respectively.

We currently rely on arrangements with two bank partners to originate a substantial portion of our loans. If our relationship with either bank partner terminates, or if either bank partner were to suspend, limit, or cease its operations or loan origination activities for any reason, and we are unable to replace the affected originations on a timely basis or at all, our business, results of operations and financial condition would be materially and adversely affected.
As of September 30, 2026, unsecured personal loans were originated in 41 states, including through our partnerships with Pathward, N.A. ("Pathward") and Column National Association ("Column").

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors); balance sheet figures from F1 (10-Q); cash flow and cost-of-debt data from P7 (8-K).
risks.claim: Oportun carries substantial leverage (total liabilities of approximately $2.78 billion against $433 million of equity) and depends on continuous access to securitization, warehouse, and corporate debt markets to fund new originations; a credit-market disruption could force curtailment of lending.
quotes: Total liabilities | 2,780,340 | 2,867,774
Total stockholders' equity | 433,439 | 390,082

We depend on securitization transactions, warehouse facilities and other forms of debt financing, as well as whole loan and structured loan sales, in order to finance the principal amount of most of the loans we make to our members.

risks.claim: The 36% APR cap on newly originated loans limits revenue upside while borrowing costs remain variable, creating asymmetric interest-rate risk that compresses net interest margin if rates rise.
quotes: We have capped the APR for newly originated loans at 36% since August 2020.
We do not currently hedge our interest rate exposure associated with our debt financing or fair market valuation of our loans.

our ability to manage impacts from, and uncertainties regarding, current and future actions that may be taken by activist stockholders

risks.basis: Stated in P5 (10-Q Risk Factors), P2 (10-K Risk Factors – model reliance), and P1 (10-K Business – AI use).
risks.claim: Oportun's reliance on proprietary A.I. and machine-learning models for underwriting, pricing, fraud detection, and savings automation creates operational, legal, regulatory, and cybersecurity risk if models fail or are subject to regulatory intervention.
quotes: Our use of and increasing reliance on A.I. technologies across our business operations may expose us to operational, legal, regulatory, cybersecurity and reputational risks.

If our credit risk models fail to adequately predict the creditworthiness of our members or their ability to repay their loans due to programming or other errors, or if any portion of the information pertaining to the potential member is incorrect, incomplete or becomes stale (whether by fraud, negligence or otherwise), and our systems do not detect such errors, inaccuracies or incomplete information, or if any portion of the credit decision process described herein fails, we may experience higher than forecasted loan losses.
we use billions of proprietary data points to score 100% of our loan applicants
